chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Yaʿqub ibn Yazid, from Marwak ibn ʿUbayd, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from a man, from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

He said to me: “What do these people say regarding a man who has missed two rakʿahs with the Imam?” He said: “They say that in the two rakʿahs he recites al-Hamd and a surah.” So he said: “This turns his salat around, making its beginning its end.” I said: “How should he act?” He said: “He recites Fatihat al-Kitab in every rakʿah.”

So this report does not contradict the reports we presented earlier, because his statement that he recites al-Hamd alone in the two rakʿahs means in the two missed rakʿahs, not in the two that he caught. For the two that he caught, he recites in them al-Hamd and a surah. For that reason, he refuted the one who said that he recites al-Hamd and a surah, for this turns his salat around, because among the common people are those who say that he recites al-Hamd and a surah in what he missed, since the two he missed were the first two, so he would need to make them up. Therefore he said in the narration of Talhah ibn Zayd: ‘And we do not say as the foolish say.’

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَانِ: the two units of prayer under discussion
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the non-Shiʿi generality whose view is being contrasted
key_terms.الْفَائِتَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs that were missed
key_terms.سُورَةٍ: an additional surah recited after al-Fatihah
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat, whose order must be preserved
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: the Opening of the Book, meaning Surat al-Fatihah

ai.seo_question: How should a person recite when making up two missed rakʿahs behind the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for one who misses two rakʿahs while praying behind the Imam and clarifies how the recitation should be performed when completing the prayer. It emphasizes preserving the proper order of the salat, so that what is made up after the Imam's completion is not treated in a way that reverses the structure of the prayer.
